clash.title: Clash check
clash.intro: Finds parts that reach into each other: steel into steel, and steel into a footing. Parts a connection joins (an end plate, its beam and the column flange it is bolted to; a base plate and its column) are meant to meet and are left out, and so are bolts and rebar. Check now looks at the phases shown.
clash.stale: The model changed since this check: Check now again.

clash.clean.one: No clashes among the 1 part checked.
clash.clean.other: No clashes among the {parts} parts and footings checked.

clash.none.one: No clashes: 1 part checked in {ms} ms.
clash.none.other: No clashes: {parts} parts and footings checked in {ms} ms.

clash.shown: {a} and {b} selected: they overlap by up to {d} mm here.
clash.note: Overlap is how far a point of one part is inside the other, up to the nearest face: a member run into a column's thin flange shows a few millimeters. A brace or beam that runs into a column with no connection is a clash: that joint still needs one.
